_source: Transcribed from reference/n8n/packages/workflow/src/workflow.ts on 2026-09-17; every value carries the line citation it was read from, and every value is corroborated by the runtime-derived group tests/reference/workflow-rust/fixtures.json `startNode` (generated by executing n8n-workflow 2.9.1 = the 2.9.4 dependency set).
_scope_warning: Plain traversal (getChildNodes/getParentNodes via graph/graph-utils.ts) does NOT filter disabled nodes — `grep -n disabled graph/graph-utils.ts` is empty. Asserting disabled-filtering in get_child_nodes/get_parent_nodes would itself be a divergence. `disabled` is behavioural ONLY in getHighestNode (workflow.ts:498, :553) and in __getStartNode (:824, :839, :853).
_registry_note: getStartNode(None) is derived under the no-registry branch: the reference's __getStartNode step that resolves nodeType.trigger/poll (workflow.ts:830-842) requires the node-type registry, which the isolated Workflow LEGO does not have. With no trigger/poll methods resolvable, the result is `null`. See docs/isolation/PHASE-3-OPENING.md.

D-01.title: disabled parent contributes nothing to getHighestNode
D-01.explains: Manual Trigger is dropped by the lenient parent check (workflow.ts:553 `disabled !== true` fails); Solo (disabled omitted) passes the same check. The climb recurses past both.

D-02.title: getStartNode(destination) uses the lenient single-candidate rule
D-02.explains: highest(Code) = ['Solo']; __getStartNode returns the single candidate when `node && !node.disabled` — omitted `disabled` qualifies.

D-03.title: final fallback returns the DISABLED node itself
D-03.explains: highest(Manual Trigger) = [] (strict :498 fails on disabled:true, no incoming connections) → candidate list is the destination alone; the single-candidate rule skips disabled nodes (:824), the STARTING_NODE_TYPES scan skips it too (:853 `disabled === true`), and the unconditional final fallback `return this.nodes[nodeNames[0]]` (:881) returns the disabled destination. Quirk preserved deliberately.

D-04.title: asymmetry: a node that OMITS disabled is never its own highest node, but IS admitted as another node's highest parent
D-04.explains: self-role is strict: :498 tests `disabled === false`, so `undefined === false` is false. parent-role is lenient: :553 tests `disabled !== true`, so `undefined !== true` is true. A port normalising both into one `!disabled` check diverges on every node lacking the field (ISSUE-017).

D-05.title: no-destination start with a disabled starting-type node yields nothing
D-05.explains: 3 candidates > 1 (single-candidate rule skipped); no registry-resolvable trigger/poll; the STARTING_NODE_TYPES scan skips Code and Solo (not starting types) and skips Manual Trigger (:853 disabled === true continue). Returns undefined.
